meta.title: The Fortune App
meta.blurb: A free app says it knows your future, and some predictions come true... Is Léo's future already written? You decide!

p1.title: The App
text: On Monday, Léo saw an ad on his phone: “FutureMe: Know your future today! It's free!” He was curious, so he downloaded the app.

text.msg: 🔮 FutureMe: It's [[going to|vai + verbo (futuro)]] rain at 4 p.m.

text: Léo laughed. The sky was blue! But at 4 p.m., it started to rain. Suddenly, Léo wasn't laughing anymore.
That night, a new [[prediction|previsão]] arrived:

text.msg: 🔮 FutureMe: You will fail the math test on Friday.

text: Léo looked at the message for a long time. Was the app right about everything?
p1.eventPt: o Léo baixou um aplicativo de previsões

question.q: What did the app predict first?

choices.label: Stop studying. It's no use!

p2a.title: Study Time
text: On Tuesday, Léo studied with his best friend, Nando. First, they did ten exercises. Then they watched a video about equations.
Nando laughed at the app. “An app can't see the future, Léo! It's only a program.”
But that night, the app sent a new message:

text.msg: 🔮 FutureMe: Do you want better predictions? Try [[premium|versão paga]]! Only R$ 20 a week.

text: Twenty reais was all his lunch money for the week.

choices.label: Pay for premium
choices.event: he paid for the premium version

choices.label: Ignore the offer
choices.event: he ignored the offer

p2b.title: No Use
text: Léo closed his math book. “Why study? The app says I will fail,” he thought. So he played video games all afternoon.
On Wednesday, his mother asked: “Are you ready for Friday's test?” Léo showed her the app. She didn't laugh.
“A phone can't decide your future, Léo,” she said. “You decide.”
That night, the app sent a new message:

text.msg: 🔮 FutureMe: Do you want better predictions? Try [[premium|versão paga]]! Only R$ 20 a week.

p3x.title: About Nando
text: On Thursday, a new prediction arrived. This time, it was about Nando.

text.msg: 🔮 FutureMe: Your friend Nando is [[going to|vai + verbo (futuro)]] lie to you tomorrow.

text: Léo looked at Nando in class. Nando was his best friend. They met when they were six years old. Was he really [[going to|vai + verbo (futuro)]] lie?
After that, Léo was quiet all day. Nando noticed. “Hey, what's wrong?” he asked.

text.text: Léo paid with his lunch money. Now he had no money for snacks, but he had premium predictions.
Léo paid with his lunch money. He didn't study anymore, so he had a lot of time for the app.

text: Léo read them again and again. They sounded important, but what did they really mean?

p3z.title: No More App
text: Léo deleted the app. First, he felt strange. Then he felt free.
He opened his math book again. It was Wednesday night, and the test was on Friday. There was very little time.
His mother smiled at the door. “Good choice,” she said. “Do you want some coffee?”
But after one hour, Léo looked at his phone again. He missed the predictions. What was the app saying about him now?

p4a.title: Two Friends, One App
text: Léo showed Nando the prediction. Nando read it, and then he laughed. He took out his own phone.
“Look!” said Nando. “I installed FutureMe yesterday, to test it. It told me the same thing!”

text.msg: 🔮 FutureMe: Your friend Léo is [[going to|vai + verbo (futuro)]] lie to you tomorrow.

text: The two friends looked at each other. The app sent the same kind of prediction to everybody. Only the names were different.

text: On Friday morning, the math test started at 7:30 a.m. The teacher, Professora Ana, gave everybody the questions.

text.text: Léo looked at the first question. He knew the answer! He studied for this.
He was tired after a night of study, but the equations were fresh in his mind.
Léo looked at the first question. He didn't know the answer. His notebook at home was empty.

p4c.title: The Secret Prediction
text: Léo had no more lunch money. So he asked his friend Nando for R$ 50.
“Fifty reais? For a prediction?” said Nando. “That's a lot of money, Léo! What is this app, really?”
Léo didn't answer. He looked at the golden button on the screen: UNLOCK YOUR SECRET PREDICTION.
Nando took out his phone. “Wait. Let's read what other people say about this app first.”

text.msg: 🔮 FutureMe: Welcome back, Léo! We missed you.

e1.title: I Decide
text: Later, Léo discovered the truth: FutureMe sent the same predictions to everybody. Nando got them. Professora Ana got them too. On the internet, thousands of users wrote the same thing: “It's a trick!”
And the rain on Monday? The app only copied the weather forecast.
Léo deleted FutureMe. Then he wrote a note in his notebook: “My future? I decide.”
e1.event: Léo discovered that the predictions were a trick
e1.eventPt: o Léo descobriu que as previsões eram um truque

question.q: Who else got the same predictions?

e2.title: Proved Wrong

text.text: After the test, Léo showed FutureMe to Professora Ana. She read the prediction and smiled. “I got the same message yesterday,” she said. “It's only a trick.”

text: The next week, Professora Ana returned the tests. Léo got 8.5! It was his best grade of the year.

text.text: That night, he cancelled the premium subscription. He wanted his lunch money back.

text: First, he took a photo of his grade. Then he opened FutureMe and wrote a review: “Your prediction was wrong. I studied, and I passed!”
Finally, he deleted the app.

e3.title: Just an App
text: Léo deleted FutureMe for good. Then he studied for one hour and went to sleep.
On Friday, the test was difficult, but not impossible. Léo got 6.0. It wasn't great, but he passed.
He never discovered how the app worked, and he didn't care. “It's just an app,” he thought.

question.q: What did Léo do with the app?
options: He showed it to the teacher

e4.title: The Premium Trap
text: Léo paid R$ 50 with Nando's money. The screen became golden, and the secret prediction appeared:

text.msg: 🔮 SECRET PREDICTION: Good things will happen to you soon.

text: That was all. Léo read it three times. He lost R$ 70 in one week: twenty for premium and fifty for one sentence.
Now he had no lunch money and a debt with Nando. It was an expensive lesson, but he learned it: when an app is free, maybe YOU are the product.
e4.event: he lost R$ 70 on the app

question.q: How much money did Léo lose?

e5.title: It Came True

text.text: After the test, Léo showed FutureMe to Professora Ana. She read the prediction and smiled. “I got the same message yesterday,” she said. “It's only a trick.”

text: The next week, Professora Ana returned the tests. Léo got 3.0.

text.text: “See? The app was right,” he said to Nando. But Nando shook his head. “No, Léo. The app didn't make you fail. You believed it, and you stopped trying.”
“The app was a trick, but I still failed,” he said to Nando. Nando shook his head. “The app didn't make you fail. You believed it, and you stopped trying.”

text: Léo looked at his empty notebook. For the first time, he understood: the prediction came true because he believed it.
e5.eventPt: o Léo foi mal na prova

options: He believed the app and stopped trying

e6.title: The Friend Who Left
text: Léo didn't laugh. “Are you [[going to|vai + verbo (futuro)]] lie to me, Nando?” he asked.
Nando stopped smiling. “Do you trust an app more than you trust me?” he said. Then he walked away.
That weekend, Nando didn't answer Léo's messages. The app didn't predict a fight, but a fight happened, and Léo started it.
